label: Food Insecure Population
contestNote: UPDATED Jul 14, 2026: UN Humanitarian Coordinator George Conway confirmed a 'real and credible risk of famine' in Burhakaba District (Bay Region) — the first district-level famine-risk confirmation of the crisis. WFP (Jun 28) reaching only 450,000 people (down from 2.2M in early 2025) as 2M enter IPC Phase 4 Emergency (double the prior year); 1.9M children face acute malnutrition; 76% of the IPC-4 population has no assistance pipeline through August. Nationally, 570,000+ need water assistance and 400,730 children face acute malnutrition (97,150 severe). HRP still only 15.2% funded as of Jul 14; over 500 health/nutrition facilities closed for lack of funds; water-trucking costs more than doubled in some areas.
delta: Burhakaba famine risk CONFIRMED (Jul 14) — first district-level famine-risk finding of the crisis; HRP still 15.2% funded
deltaNote: UN (Jul 14, 2026): 'The humanitarian context in Somalia is worsening faster than we originally projected... without immediate and sustained support from donors, the diaspora and the private sector, we risk a preventable catastrophe.' Somalia Humanitarian Fund allocated $4.7M to Burhakaba (incl. $2M reserve). No confirmed WFP full operational shutdown, but reach has fallen to roughly 1-in-5 of the early-2025 caseload.

label: AUSSOM Authorized Strength
delta: UNSOS drawdown now visibly underway: staff terminations and asset auctions began the week of Aug 25
deltaNote: In a July 1, 2026 letter to the African Union, the US said it will not support UNSOS — AUSSOM's logistics backbone (fuel, medevac, food, engineering, COE reimbursement) — beyond Dec 31, 2026, and will oppose any UNSC renewal including UNSOS support. Cites Somalia's failure to take ownership of security despite ~$2B in UNSOS support plus $1.6B bilateral aid over a decade. AU Commission convened an emergency meeting; a senior African diplomat called the decision 'irreversible.' UPDATED Aug 25-26, 2026 (Radio Dalsan / WardheerNews): the drawdown moved from planning to execution — at least 10 civilian AU-UN Information Support Team staff received termination notices effective Sep 10, and UNSOS began auctioning vehicles, generators, medical supplies and other equipment. UNTMIS separately remains on track to complete transition to a standard UN country team by Oct 31, 2026. Security Council Report (Jun 2026) separately noted AUSSOM had expanded to 49 locations (vs. 23 in the original operational concept), reflecting drawdown pause/reversal.

label: Piracy Hostages (Simultaneous, 2026)
source: UnHerd Aug 10, 2026 / Maritime Executive Aug 17-18, 2026 / AP Aug 20-22, 2026 / IMO
contestNote: UnHerd (Aug 10, 2026) reported 67 seafarers held hostage across 4 ships, up from the 44 hostages/3 vessels figure confirmed as of mid-July — the increase reflects additional hijackings and crew additions not yet individually itemized in this tracker. A 5th vessel, the Cameroon-flagged cargo ship Lutuf, was hijacked off Mareeyo on Aug 17, 2026 (crew reported safe; count pending confirmation from UKMTO/EU NAVFOR). A 6th vessel, the Eritrean-flagged tanker Sibu 1 (also reported as Seamull), was hijacked in the Gulf of Aden on Aug 20, 2026 with 20 crew aboard (16 Indian, plus Syrian, Sudanese and Iraqi nationals), steered toward Puntland's coast — AP reported it as the sixth commercial vessel hijacked by Somali pirates since April 2026. A combined post-Sibu 1 hostage total has not yet been re-published by IMO/EU NAVFOR, so the headline figure remains the pre-Sibu-1 count. Honour 25 (hijacked Apr 2026) remains held with a £3M ransom demand outstanding.
delta: Sixth vessel hijacked since April (Sibu 1/Seamull, Aug 20) as Djibouti Code of Conduct states move to launch a joint counter-piracy task force
deltaNote: Maritime Executive (Aug 17-18) reported the Lutuf hijacking prompted regional states to accelerate plans for a new Combined Task Force under the Djibouti Code of Conduct, citing thinned EU NAVFOR/CTF-151 patrol coverage. The Aug 20 Sibu 1/Seamull hijacking underscores the pattern continuing unabated. No ransom paid or hostages released on any held vessel as of Aug 22.
